title: Joining ideas: and, but, although, unless
goal: Connect ideas with the right joining word, used once
intro: Joining words (conjunctions) link ideas. And adds, but contrasts, so gives a result, because gives a reason. Although and though show contrast in one clause, unless means “if not”, and until means “up to the time when”. Use only one joining word between two clauses.

examples: It was late, so we took a taxi.
I stayed because I was tired.

rules.rule: although / though / even though: contrast. Never add “but”.
examples: Although it was expensive, I bought it.
I went out even though it was raining.

rules.rule: unless = if not. until = up to the time.
examples: You won’t pass unless you study.

rules.rule: both … and, either … or, neither … nor, not only … but also.
examples: She speaks both Hindi and Tamil.
Either call me or text me.

mistakes.wrong: Although he tried, but he failed.
Unless you don’t hurry, you’ll miss it.
mistakes.right: Unless you hurry, you’ll miss it.

mistakes.wrong: Both my brother as well as my sister are doctors.
mistakes.right: Both my brother and my sister are doctors.

mistakes.wrong: Not only he sings but dances.
mistakes.right: He not only sings but also dances.

ex.q: ___ it was raining, the match continued.
You can’t come in ___ you have a ticket.
I was hungry, ___ I made some noodles.
Though she is young, but she is very wise.
ex.fixed: Though she is young, she is very wise.

ex.q: Unless you don't reply, I will call.
ex.fixed: Unless you reply, I will call.

ex.q: Neither my father or my mother drives.
ex.fixed: Neither my father nor my mother drives.

ex.q: I’ll take either tea ___ coffee, whatever is ready.

ex.a: I went to work even though I was sick.

ex.q: Join with “although”: “It was expensive. I bought it.”
a: Although it was expensive I bought it
I bought it although it was expensive
ex.y: Although it was expensive, I bought it.

talk: Talk about a difficult decision you made. Use although, because, so, unless, and until to explain your thinking.
